newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares shed 1.77pct in volatile session.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares shed 1.77pct in volatile session.

text.p: Greek stocks traded in negative territory but managed to trim mid-session losses of over 2.1 percent after a broad-based retreat and settle 1.77 percent lower in heavy volume.

"Consolidation or even sharp drops are more than welcome for repositioning. Profit-taking in banks and blue chips is likely to continue but even a 10 percent retreat is not worrisome because we are in a bull market," said analyst Emmanuel Varsos at Investment Analysis.

Following the first wave of euphoria which propelled the benchmark share index 31.2 percent higher since the start of the year, the Athens bourse will become increasingly a stock pickers market, he forecast.
"Players should take advantage of corrections and be on the buy side. But buying the index is not necessarily going to be the solution henceforth," he said.

And in a sobering assessment after a recent ING Barings bullish viewpoint, Merrill Lynch analyst Mike Harris told Reuters he saw limited upside potential for Greek equities and a risk-reward profile that was not compelling.

"Greek equities fall firmly in the sell territory of European emerging markets when weighing P/E levels versus estimated EPS growth," he said, adding that there was room for the index to give back about one third of its gains.

Varsos found the outlook for a correction reasonable but stressed that CPI inflation which fell to a record low 6.8 percent in December will be on a sustained downtrend at least until April, regardless of moves in the dollar and oil prices.

"I agree with Mr. Harris that a 10 percent correction could be in the works. However, this is more than welcome because we are in a bull market. The market's after-tax P/E ratio on 1997 earnings is 9.5 compared to a P/E of 10 for T-bills," he said.
Meanwhile during a press conference, Prime Minister Costas Simitis reiterated that Greece would part-float the Public Petroleum Corporation DEP by year-end 1997.
The Athens general share index settled 1.77 percent or 22.17 points lower at 1230.20 points from Wednesday's 1252.37, after opening at 1251.00.
Losers led gainers 171 to 55 with 23 issues unchanged on 249 traded. Turnover was 17.0 billion drachmas on volume of 5.4 million shares.
Banks fell 2.21 percent along with construction, down 3.0 percent and industrials, off 1.95 percent. Leasing shares dropped 1.6 percent with small-caps ending 0.32 percent weaker.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 968.00-986.00. Shares of OTE telecom the underlying, ended unchanged at 5,750.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted lower at $26.22-$27.48. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted lower at 9,354-9,939 drachmas.
